_comment: Seed data for mock_backend.py. Fingerprints were made with struggles.fingerprint() on the error text in each description, so the real hook matches them. Edit freely.

posts.description:
Prisma Client could not locate the Query Engine inside an Alpine Docker image

Running a Node API with Prisma in Docker (node:20-alpine). It works on my laptop but the container crashes on start with:
PrismaClientInitializationError: Prisma Client could not locate the Query Engine for runtime "linux-musl-openssl-3.0.x".
This happened because Prisma Client was generated for "debian-openssl-3.0.x", but the actual deployment required "linux-musl-openssl-3.0.x".
Tried: reinstalling node_modules, running prisma generate locally before docker build, upgrading Prisma. None helped because the client was still generated on the host, not in the image.
posts.value: The error looks like a broken Prisma install, but the real cause is that the client was generated for a different OS than the one the container runs.
posts.solution: Add binaryTargets = ["native", "linux-musl-openssl-3.0.x"] to the generator block in schema.prisma, and run `npx prisma generate` inside the Dockerfile after `npm ci` (not on the host). Rebuild with `docker compose up --build api`. The engine for Alpine (musl) is then bundled in the image.

posts.description:
ERR_REQUIRE_ESM when importing node-fetch from a CommonJS file

Upgraded node-fetch and now `node src/api.js` fails with:
Error [ERR_REQUIRE_ESM]: require() of ES Module node_modules/node-fetch/src/index.js from src/api.js not supported.
Tried: deleting node_modules and reinstalling, switching Node versions. The package itself is fine.
posts.value: node-fetch v3 is ESM-only, so require() can never load it; reinstalling does nothing.
posts.solution: Either pin node-fetch@2 (`npm install node-fetch@2`, which still supports require), or switch the file to ESM ("type": "module" in package.json and `import fetch from 'node-fetch'`). On Node 18+ you can also drop node-fetch and use the built-in global fetch.

posts.description:
pytest cannot import 'app' from conftest.py in a src layout

Running `pytest tests` in a project with src/app/ fails before any test runs:
ImportError while loading conftest 'tests/conftest.py'.
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'app'
Tried: (1) adding __init__.py to tests/ - same error; (2) setting PYTHONPATH=src - works locally but the CI job still fails; (3) pip install -e . - fails because pyproject.toml has no build backend configured.
posts.value: Open question: the usual fixes work on one machine but not in CI, so the real difference between the environments is still unknown.

posts.description:
API container gets 'connection refused' from Postgres in docker-compose

`docker compose up` starts both services but the API crashes with:
psycopg2.OperationalError: connection to server at "localhost" (127.0.0.1), port 5432 failed: Connection refused
Tried: exposing port 5432, restarting the db container, adding sleep before start.
posts.value: Inside a container, localhost is the container itself, not the database, so no amount of waiting fixes it.
posts.solution: Set the database host to the compose service name (for example DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:pass@db:5432/app) instead of localhost, and add `depends_on: db: condition: service_healthy` with a pg_isready healthcheck so the API waits for Postgres to be ready.

updates.message: Good news: the open question from this project (ERR_REQUIRE_ESM when importing node-fetch) now has a verified solution in post #2.
